Heard Sri.Mahendra G., learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri.Vinayaka V.S., learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent.

3. Brief facts of the case are as under:
A complaint came to be lodged by Smt.Bharathi, wife of Govardhan, with Rajagopal Nagar Police Station, Bangalore City on 03.05.2022 which was registered in Crime No.140/2022 for the offence punishable under Section 5(L), 6; IPC of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (for short 'POCSO') 1860.

sentences.text:
The gist of the complaint averments would reveal that the daughter of the complainant being aged about five years was visiting each and every house in the vicinity for playing and likewise she used to visit the house of the accused/petitioner as well.
5. On 02.05.2022 at about 4.00 p.m., the daughter of the complainant came home back and intimated the complainant that the accused/petitioner mis-behaved with the victim girl by kissing her on forehead and disrobing her and touched the private parts and other parts of the body of the victim girl and also touching his private part on the body of the victim girl.
6.
Immediately, thereafter, complainant went to the house of the accused/petitioner around 7.00 p.m. and he was not found.

On the next day morning around 8.00 a.m. complainant again went to the house of the petitioner and he was found and there was a commotion in the area and the general public have beaten the accused and he escaped from the scene.

7. After registering the case, Police have investigated the matter inter-alia apprehended the petitioner and after his medical examination he has been sent to the judicial custody.
8.
After thorough investigation, Police have filed charge sheet against the petitioner for the aforesaid offences.

9. In the meantime, the attempt made by the petitioner to obtain an order of grant of bail is turned-down by the Additional City Civil and Sessions Judge-FTSC-II, Bengaluru in Criminal Misc No.9822/2022 vide order dated 25.11.2022

entities.text: Additional City Civil and Sessions Judge-FTSC-II, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Thereafter, the petitioner is before this Court.

10. Reiterating the grounds urged in the petition, learned counsel for the petitioner Sri.Mahendra G., vehemently contended that the case of the prosecution is hollow enough in view of the fact that the medical report does not make-out a case of sexual assault and at the most, offences alleged against the petitioner even if it stands proved may be traceable under Section 7 of POCSO Act and punishable under Section 8 of the POCSO Act

and as such the gravity of the offences alleged against the petitioner has been reduced to a considerable extent and sought for grant of bail.
11.

He also pointed out that the material on record especially the contradictory statements of the father and mother of the victim girl itself is enough to enlarge the petitioner on bail and this is not a case where custodial trail is utmost necessary and sought for grant of bail.

12. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader vehemently opposes the bail grounds contending that the statement of the victim girl is sufficient enough to attract the offences alleged under Section 5(L) of the POCSO Act and the age of the victim girl being 5 years, there is every possibility of tampering the prosecution witness, if the petitioner is enlarged on bail.

And therefore,
sought for rejection of bail.

13. Perused the material on record meticulously in view of the rival contentions of the parties.

sentences.text: On such perusal of the material on record, it is seen that the victim girl is aged 5 years.

On 02.05.2022, the victim girl as usual visited the house of the accused and came back to the her house and intimated her mother that the accused/petitioner has mis-behaved with her by kissing on her forehead and also touching her private parts and the petitioner touched his private part on all parts of the body including the private parts of the victim.
15.
Immediately around 7.00 p.m. on the same day, complainant along with her daughter visited the house of the petitioner and he was not found and
on the next day morning i.e., on 03.05.2022 again the complainant visited the house of the petitioner with the victim girl, at that time the petitioner was traced.
On hearing of the incident there was commotion in the locality an the general public and caught hold of the petitioner and beaten him up and the petitioner some how escaped from the place.
16. After registering the case, Police have thoroughly investigated the matter and filed charge sheet.
17. No doubt the medical report of the victim girl does not make-out a case for a penetrative sexual assault as much as hymn is intact.

Anyway whether the sexual assault or penetrative sexual assault or aggravated penetrative sexual assault has taken place to the victim girl or not cannot be decided by this Court at this stage by holding a mini trial.

18. Suffice to say that the statement of the victim girl recorded by the Police Sub-Inspector during the course of the investigation would prima-facie establish the ingredients to attract the offences alleged against the accused/petitioner.
19.

As rightly contended by the learned High Court Government Pleader, since the age of the victim girl is aged 5 years, atleast till the examination of the victim girl and the complainant before the trial Court, if the petitioner is enlarged on bail, there is every possibility of tampering the prosecution witness.

18. The other aspects of the matter argued on behalf of the petitioner would be resulting in holding a mini trial to find out the merits or de-merits of the case which is deprecated in catena of judgments as the same would prejudice the case of the parties during the trial one or the other way.

20. Suffice to say that on perusal of the material on record at this stage with regard to the presumption available to the prosecution under Sections 29 and 30 of POCSO Act, the grounds urged in petition is hardly sufficient in obtaining an order of grant of bail by resorting to the special powers vested in this Court under Section 439 Cr.P.C.
Hence, following order is passed:
ORDER
The Criminal petition is rejected.
